Brand identity · Visual system

Where heritage meets horizon.

A visual identity connecting the region’s architecture, sun, and golden dunes.

My roleVisual Designer
ScopeLogo exploration, brand guidelines, applications
Tools & methodsSketching, visual identity, layout design

01 / The brief

A place, expressed through an identity.

This tourism identity brings Rajasthan’s architecture, warm landscape, and cultural character into one visual system. The aim was to create a recognizable mark that could travel consistently between a brand book, stationery, and visitor-facing objects.

02 / Sketching & exploration

Starting with pencil, shape, and place.

The original sketches explore ways to combine architectural silhouettes, the sun, desert forms, and lettering. Seeing the alternatives together reveals the move from individual regional cues toward a compact, unified symbol.

03 / The final direction

Four elements. One visual story.

The final logo brings together the sun, forts, desert, and Rajasthan logotype. The architectural forms reference historic forts; the sun and desert connect the identity to the region’s warm climate and golden dunes. The composition carries these references into a single recognizable mark.

04 / Building the system

Guidelines that make the identity repeatable.

Warm reds, terracotta, orange, and sand tones form the palette, supported by black and white. The guidelines define typography, color use, size, clearspace, and treatments to avoid. Clearspace uses the x-height of the “n” in the logotype, giving the mark a consistent area to breathe.

05 / Across touchpoints

From the page to the objects people keep.

Letterheads and business cards extend the identity into everyday communication. Badges, mugs, and apparel show how the same mark and palette can retain their character across different sizes, materials, and contexts.

Outcome / What changed

One identity, ready to work across different touchpoints.

The project translated separate regional references into a unified logo and a documented visual system. Clearspace, typography, color, and usage rules made the identity repeatable across stationery and merchandise, with applications shown below. The result is a complete identity system; tourism awareness or visitor-impact figures were not measured in this project.
